9.0.0.en: Before Christ sent His disciples out to serve, He gave them authority over the demons and all their works in human beings, so that they might cast them out and deliver people from them, and also heal all diseases.

9.0.1.en: If God calls you to His service, be confident that He gives you His power first, and no obstacle stands before you, not even the demons, because our God is able to do all things, and it is He who works in you when you serve Him.

9.1.0.en: The aim of the service is to proclaim God's reign over hearts and repentance from every sin, so that the heart may become pure and fit for God to dwell in. He joined this proclamation with the healing of diseases as a confirmation of the power of these teachings, and because we are in the body and not spirits only, we need spiritual teaching joined with support for the body, that is, its healing from diseases.

9.2.0.en: Christ declared to His disciples that they have no need of material resources in His service, because God, who gave them authority over the demons and diseases, is sufficient for all their needs. So they do not need a (staff) to lean on or to defend themselves with, because Christ defends them with His Cross, the true staff. Nor do they need a (scrip) in which food is put, because Christ is their true food and gives them their needs of material bread. Nor the money of the world (silver), for He enriches them, and they have no need of (coats), for He clothes them with the garment of righteousness, and preserves their material garments, and compensates them for everything material that is lost.

9.3.0.en: He also commanded them not to move from house to house for the sake of courtesies and hospitality, but to stay in one house in order to concentrate on their aim, which is preaching, and in this there is no burden on that house because they stay only a short time in each village.

9.4.0.en: Christ warned them that some would reject their teachings, and they should not be disturbed, but shake off the dust from their feet, that is, take nothing material from them, not even the dust, and continue preaching to others.

9.5.0.en: The beautiful thing is that they cared for every village or small place and offered it the service of preaching and healing. Do not neglect anyone, however small or weak he may seem, but offer the love of Christ to all, for among them are the brethren of God, and this rejoices His heart greatly.

9.6.0.en: Herod Antipas was tetrarch of Galilee, the son of Herod the Great, and he heard of the preaching of Christ and His disciples and was perplexed because of some sayings spread among the people that John was risen from the dead, while others said that Elijah, who had ascended to heaven, had appeared on earth, and others thought that Christ was one of the old prophets, such as Isaiah, who had risen and begun to preach.

9.7.0.en: Herod admitted his crime, which was the killing of John, and wondered whether he had truly risen from the dead. His fear of John's rebukes of him was still great, and he desired to see Christ to be sure of this. I hear of Him such things -: that is, the mighty miracles of Christ.

9.7.1.en: Sin troubles the sinner, and the word of truth goes on echoing even after the death of the one who spoke it; so regain your peace by repentance so that you are not disturbed by the truth.

9.8.0.en: After the disciples returned from the service on which Christ had sent them, they came to Him and told Him all that had happened to them, and then Christ withdrew with His disciples by way of the sea to the city of Bethsaida, and came to the plain adjoining the city to rest with His disciples in this desert place.

9.8.1.en: It is important that you give a report of your service to the One who sent you, that is, God, with prayer and thanksgiving, and also to the one responsible for your service, so that he may follow you up and guide you.

9.9.0.en: The crowds of the Jews heard of His presence, and hurried to Him, and He welcomed them, and neither He nor His disciples sought their own rest, but He seized it as an opportunity to satisfy them with His life-giving word and to heal those who sought healing from their diseases. We notice that Christ prepared the crowds by His word, and cleansed them of their weariness and diseases, before they ate of the food He blessed (the fish and the bread).

9.9.1.en: As happens today in partaking of the Holy Mysteries, we must prepare ourselves with spiritual teachings through the Liturgy of the Catechumens and all the prayers of the Liturgy, and be cleansed in the sacrament of repentance and confession; then we are made worthy to receive the Holy Mysteries.

9.9.2.en: God gives you, if you feel your need of Him and ask of Him.

9.10.0.en: From the sweetness of Christ's word and His care for healing all diseases, the time lengthened until sunset, and the disciples felt the hunger of the crowds and their need of rest, so they asked Christ to send them away so that they might return to their villages where they would find food and a place to rest, because the plain where they had gathered was outside the cities and villages. Here the care of the servants, that is, the disciples, for those they serve appears.

9.11.0.en: Christ responded with concern to the crowds' need of food, and asked His disciples to look for food to feed the crowds. They searched and found only five loaves and two fishes with a lad, and then they told Christ that they had no food, and that if He wished, the disciples could go and buy food for the crowds from the surrounding villages. This is the last of human capabilities, namely weakness and helplessness before the greatness of the problem; they recognized it but had no solution, since they also did not have the money to buy this food.

9.12.0.en: The number of the crowds was great, five thousand men besides women and children, and the number of women and children was not mentioned because the man is the head of the family and so points to it; that is, those who ate were 5000 families.

9.12.1.en: The omission of women and children is not out of contempt for them, but symbolizes spiritually that the woman points to the life of luxury and the child to immaturity, while the man points to the serious life and the bearing of responsibility. The number five points to the five books of Moses, that is, all the Jews, and a thousand points to eternity and the heavenly life, so the five thousand point to the Jews who believe in Christ and live with a heavenly mind. The five loaves point to the five senses, as the scholar Origen says, that is, the completeness of human effort. The two fishes are a symbol of the Old and New Testaments, so they offered to Christ human effort in its great weakness in the two Testaments, and He by His blessing made it abundant and sufficient to satisfy.

9.12.2.en: As the weakness of man appears, the power of Christ and His divinity appear, who began to solve the problem, and He commanded the disciples to divide the crowds into companies, each company of fifty, and by this order the food could reach everyone, and the greatness of the blessing appears in their being satisfied.

9.12.3.en: The number five, as we said, points to human effort, and ten is the number of perfection, so fifty signifies the perfection of human effort, which is merely dividing them into companies, while the satisfaction comes from the grace of Christ.

9.13.0.en: The disciples and the crowd obeyed, and here the importance of order and obedience appears. Then Christ took the two fishes and the five loaves, that is, the small gift of men, and looked up to heaven to lift hearts to the heavenly life and to declare that He is God who came from heaven to redeem them, and then He blessed the food and broke it, and the blessing continued until they distributed it to all the crowd.

9.14.0.en: All ate and were filled, and there was more than enough, so Christ commanded that the fragments be gathered, to make them feel the overflow of the blessing so that we do not neglect it or throw it away, and the fragments were many, so that they filled twelve baskets, corresponding to the number of the disciples or the number of the tribes of Israel, that is, the blessing is sufficient for all believers, and as each disciple carries a basket on his shoulder while returning to the city, he is assured in his heart of the power and blessing of the miracle.

9.15.0.en: Christ was alone with His disciples in a quiet place, and offered a prayer for their faith in Him and to teach them the importance of prayer and solitude. In proportion to the importance of the service, it ought to be preceded by prayer and solitude to be filled with God. Then Christ asked His disciples what people thought of Him, to show human thought and its limits, and to encourage them afterward to declare their faith in Him, which is higher than the faith of the crowds.

9.16.0.en: The opinions of the Jews differed, for some thought He was John risen from the dead or Elijah come down from heaven, because of His power in declaring the truth like theirs, and because of His profound words others thought He was one of the prophets of the Old Testament who had risen and begun to preach again.

9.17.0.en: The Christ of God: the One anointed by God for the redemption of mankind.

9.17.1.en: Christ asked His disciples about their faith in Him, after they had been discipled at His hands and understood Him more than the crowds, who still lived with a limited, earthly human mind.

9.17.2.en: So Peter, being bold, declared the thought of the disciples about Christ, that He is the awaited Messiah, of whom the prophecies spoke.

9.18.0.en: Christ forbade them to declare this to the crowds so that they would not be occupied with Him as an earthly king, since the mistaken belief of the Jews about the Christ was that His kingdom was earthly and would deliver them from the Romans, and He made clear to His disciples that He must suffer and die and afterward rise victorious, for the Messiah is the Redeemer and Savior who dies for us to raise us up in Him.

9.18.1.en: Accept to suffer with Christ first, so that you may enjoy His power and resurrection in your life, and do not be occupied with people's opinion of you lest you be hindered from your aim, which is the Kingdom.

9.19.0.en: After Christ declared to His disciples the necessity of His suffering and death for mankind, it seems that He reached one of the villages with His disciples and the crowds came out to meet Him, and He declared to them also an essential condition for His followers, namely taking up the cross, through humility and denial of self, and then bearing sufferings and afflictions also, not only at certain times or at the beginning of life with God, but as an essential mark of the believer's life every day.

9.20.0.en: Whoever saves his life is concerned with satisfying his lusts and his bodily comfort and running after honor. He loses it: by this he draws away from God and is enslaved to his body, and nothing awaits him but eternal destruction. Christ gladdens the hearts of His hearers in that taking up the cross is the salvation of the soul, for to the extent of bearing the cross and crushing the self, the soul is delivered from sin and enjoys fellowship with Christ, and then receives eternal salvation.

9.21.0.en: The meaning of taking up the cross is giving up the corrupt pleasures of the world, because the soul and its salvation are more precious than the whole world

9.22.0.en: Whoever refuses to take up the cross and is ashamed to bear disgrace, insults and sufferings, Christ also will be ashamed of him on the Day of Judgment before the angels and the saints, that is, he will be cast into torment and lose all the glory of the children of God. So taking up the cross is an essential condition for salvation and eternal glory.

9.23.0.en: Christ concludes His words by saying that His salvation will soon be made known by His death and resurrection, and everyone who accepts taking up the cross will believe in Him and He will reign over his heart, and so many of His hearers will see the Kingdom of God in the hearts of believers. There is another interpretation, that He means the revelation of His glory on the Mount of Transfiguration to three of His disciples. And a third interpretation, the spread of the Gospel throughout the whole world within not many years at the hands of the Apostles, so that God reigns over the hearts of believers spread throughout the whole world.

9.23.1.en: The meaning of this is to encourage His hearers to take up the cross to obtain His reign over their hearts and then the eternal Kingdom. Accept the sufferings that meet you, for they are by God's permission for the growth of your spiritual life and your deliverance from many sins, and have recourse to God in the midst of these sufferings, so that your faith is established and you experience fellowship with Him more than before.

9.24.0.en: Eight days after His talk about the sufferings and the crucifixion (counting the day on which He spoke of the crucifixion and the day on which He was transfigured, and so this is two days more than Matthew and Mark mention, for they said after six days (Mt 17:1).

9.24.1.en: The number 8 points to eternity, because the days of the week are 7, so the day after them brings us into what lies beyond this life, that is, eternity, and this is because the Transfiguration is a glimpse of the glories of heaven.

9.24.2.en: Christ took His three close disciples, because of their special spiritual readiness to receive great divine revelations and their eagerness and joy to be with Christ as much as possible, and He went up with them to a mountain, which was most likely Mount Hermon.

9.24.3.en: The mountain is a symbol of carrying out the commandment, so spiritual striving is needed to rise from earthly things to heavenly things, by carrying out the commandment and bearing the toils of the ascent, to enjoy God's blessing and His revealing Himself to us as we carry out His commandments.

9.24.4.en: The purpose first declared to the disciples was prayer in solitude with Christ, and since they loved solitude and prayer, Christ revealed His glory to them in the Transfiguration.

9.24.5.en: God is ready to reveal Himself to you if you love to be with Him in prayer and strive to carry out His commandments.

9.25.0.en: Christ did not leave His humanity, but was changed, that is, became glorified, for He is God incarnate, and His divinity did not cause Him to lose His humanity.

9.25.1.en: Christ's raiment is a symbol of the Church, which clings to Him, and so becomes white from the brightness of His glory and His work in her. So our glory comes through our clinging to Him.

9.26.0.en: Moses and Elijah appeared with Christ in His transfiguration in the form of two men. Moses represents the Law and Elijah represents the prophets, for Christ is the end of the Law and the prophets and the hope of those who have fallen asleep like Moses, and of the living who strive like Elijah.

9.27.0.en: Moses and Elijah appeared with Christ transfigured in inexpressible glory, in order that Christ might reveal something of His eternal divinity and the glory of His saints in Him, and the subject of the conversation was the redemption that He would accomplish by the Cross at Jerusalem, since this is the aim of the Law and the prophets and of Christ's Incarnation. The Transfiguration does not distract us from the Cross, but the Cross is the way to complete the divine love for mankind so that it may be glorified in Him.

9.27.1.en: If you want Christ to be transfigured in your heart, bear His sufferings so that you may experience His love.

9.28.0.en: The three disciples could not bear the greatness of Christ's glory in His transfiguration, and His light, which is brighter than the sun in its shining as Matthew and Mark mention in their Gospels, so they slept through the weakness of the flesh and heard only a little of Christ's conversation with Moses and Elijah, and when they awoke they found the scene as it was, that is, Christ in great glory.

9.29.0.en: The disciples noticed that Moses and Elijah were about to depart, and from the excess of their joy at the sight of the Transfiguration they wished they could remain in it always. So Peter, expressing this, wished to make three tabernacles for Christ, Moses and Elijah, so that they might remain before the disciples in this great sight.

9.29.1.en: A person makes a shelter to protect him from the heat and light of the sun, but now the light was shining from Christ Himself, so how would He need a shelter? But Peter did not grasp all this, because the glory of the Transfiguration had overwhelmed him, for it is beyond the understanding of the mind.

9.29.2.en: Enjoying Christ in solitude and His transfiguration to you does not make you forget to return to your service and bear sufferings; rather, the Transfiguration is a divine revelation that supports you in the toils of service and the sufferings of life.

9.30.0.en: The glory of the Transfiguration was too great for the three disciples to bear any longer, so a cloud overshadowed them, and they feared as they entered into it and lost sight of everything around them. The cloud points to the presence of God, as happened with Moses on the mountain when he received the Law.

9.31.0.en: What increased their awe was hearing the voice of God declaring that Christ is His only Son, and commanding them to hear His teachings so that they might be saved, for He is the only Son in essence, revealed to mankind to redeem it, and this same testimony had preceded at Christ's baptism in the Jordan (Mt 3:17).

9.32.0.en: After that the disciples found themselves alone with Christ, for Moses and Elijah had departed and the cloud had vanished, and the disciples told no one of the Transfiguration until after His resurrection as Christ commanded them (this is mentioned in the Gospel of Matthew), because of the weakness of the crowds' faith, for they would not understand or grasp His divinity and His transfiguration.

9.33.s.en: (7) The casting out of a devil from the only son of his father

9.33.0.en: The Transfiguration was probably at night, and on the morning of the next day Christ had come down from the mountain with the three disciples, and found the crowds who loved His teachings and needed healing from His hands waiting for Him with the nine remaining disciples.

9.34.0.en: A father came forward to Christ who had an only son whom the devil had entered, so that he lost his mind and balance and would cry out at times and at other times fall to the ground unconscious with saliva running from his mouth like the foam of the sea (froth), and this person would strike himself on the ground many times by the devil's action so that his body was full of bruises (bruising him), and with difficulty the devil would leave him for a little and then return and throw him down again, so his torment was severe and the father's heart was torn for his son, therefore he asked Christ to look upon him, confident of His fatherhood and tenderness. Trust in God's tenderness and set your troubles before Him in prayer, for His fatherhood answers you in proportion to your humility and faith.

9.35.0.en: The father complained to Christ of the disciples' inability to cast the devil out of his son.

9.36.0.en: Christ revealed the reason the devil did not come out, which was the weakness of this father's faith, like the weakness of the faith of the rest of the crowds, in addition to the weakness of the disciples' faith; He also revealed the reason the devil enters people, which is their wickedness and their distance from God. Then He told the man to bring his son before Christ that He might heal him.

9.37.0.en: While they were bringing this son, before he came near to Christ, the devil threw him down, and he fell on the ground in a faint, and here Christ rebuked him by the authority of His divinity, and the devil came out and the son was healed, and He gave him back to his father.

9.38.0.en: The miracle of casting out the devil was great because of the evil state the son was in, and the disciples were amazed together with the crowds. Perhaps the disciples' thinking turned to the nearness of Christ's declaring Himself a king and savior of the Jews from the Roman occupation, so Christ drew their attention to the aim of His Incarnation, which is redemption and not the display of His glory, because He is God glorified from eternity.

9.39.0.en: Christ reminded His disciples of His earlier talk with them about His sufferings and His crucifixion at the hands of men, for this is the purpose of the Incarnation.

9.40.0.en: The disciples did not understand the reason for Christ's suffering, being absorbed in their wish that Christ would reign on earth and glorify them with Him, and from their amazement at His authority over the demons they were afraid to ask Him the meaning of His being delivered into the hands of men and His bearing many sufferings even to death.

9.40.1.en: Do not immerse yourself in your material ambitions and the lusts of the world, lest the sight of the truth and the knowledge of God and sound conduct be hidden from you, and then you become exposed to distress from many things.

9.41.s.en: (9) Teaching humility by setting a child

9.41.0.en: Sadly, the disciples did not understand Christ's words about His sufferings and crucifixion and the necessity that His followers take up the cross after Him, because of their being influenced by the Jewish thought about the Messiah, that He reigns a material kingdom and glorifies them with Him. Therefore they reasoned and discussed who would be greatest in this earthly kingdom.

9.42.0.en: They did not tell Christ what they had discussed, since they were ashamed of it, but Christ by His divinity knew their thoughts and their fall into the sin of pride in seeking material greatness, so He offered them a solution by setting a child in their midst, who represents humility and innocence, for it is easy for a child to declare his need and weakness before all.

9.43.0.en: The least among you: the humble one, like the child.

9.43.1.en: Great, glorified and exalted in the sight of God, and he will have a higher place in heaven.

9.43.2.en: Christ honored childhood, which the Romans and Greeks despised at that time, and the Jews also, for He regarded receiving and honoring a child as receiving Him, and whoever receives Christ receives Him that sent Him, to affirm that He and God are one. And receiving care for the child is an offering of the humility apparent in him, and this humility is the cause of true greatness in the sight of God.

9.43.3.en: Contemplate the qualities of children and learn from their conduct so that you may acquire humility.

9.44.s.en: (10) Forbidding one who casts out devils

9.44.0.en: The beloved John thought that the working of miracles was confined to Christ's disciples, so when he saw with the rest of the disciples a person casting out devils, they forbade him because he was not one of the disciples. This shows that the love of preeminence and pride, which Christ tried to cure in the preceding verses, was still within the disciples.

9.45.0.en: Christ answered John by declaring an important principle in Christianity, namely love for all and appreciation of every good work, such as giving relief to a person by driving demons away from him even if the one who does this work is not connected with us. For God works in whomever He sees fit, but this does not mean that we follow everyone who does good without discernment. We do not attack heretics, for example, except in their heresy, but as for the good that they do, we do not stand against it, while taking care not to be deceived by them.

9.45.1.en: I wish you would learn a virtue from every person you meet, even one who is far from the Church, for God works in all to draw all to Himself, and your learning virtues from others moves you to love them, teaches you humility and makes you grow spiritually.

9.46.0.en: When the end of Christ's life on earth drew near, through His crucifixion and death and then His resurrection and ascension, He set out traveling from Galilee to Jerusalem where He would suffer, for His being taken up is His being lifted up on the Cross, and then His being lifted up by the Ascension.

9.46.1.en: And He did not travel directly to Jerusalem, but spent a few months in Perea east of the Jordan, and the events that took place in this period are recorded in the following ten chapters, and the Gospel of Luke alone records them, except for a few events that Luke mentioned but at another time, because Luke does not concern himself with chronological order.

9.46.2.en: If sufferings await you, do not draw back from your responsibility so as to fulfil your aims, and be confident that God supports you in every good work you do.

9.47.0.en: Christ drew near to Samaria, and sent some of His disciples before Him to one of the villages of Samaria, to prepare a house in which He might stay and preach.

9.48.0.en: The Samaritans refused to let this Jew (Christ) enter and stay with them, because they hate the Jews, since from the eighth century before the birth of Christ they had mixed with the pagans who migrated to them from the lands of the Assyrian kingdom, and had turned away from the worship of God in Jerusalem. Perhaps they rejected Christ because of His concern for worship in Jerusalem and not on Mount Gerizim, where they pray.

9.48.1.en: And God permitted them to reject Him so that He might complete His journey to Jerusalem and accomplish redemption by His sufferings and crucifixion.

9.49.0.en: James and John were enraged by the Samaritans' insult to Christ in refusing His entry among them, so they thought to take vengeance on them by fire coming down from heaven to consume them, basing this thought on what Elijah did to the servants of King Ahaziah, when he brought down fire that consumed them as they came to arrest him (2 Kgs 1:10-11)

9.50.0.en: Christ rejected the words of James and John, that is, rejected the spirit of vengeance in them, and made clear that He had become incarnate to save the world, whereas in the case of Elijah in the Old Testament, God wanted to show by his hands the weakness of idol worship, and that He is the only God able to destroy all the wicked who follow the worship of idols. Then Christ departed to continue His preaching quietly in another village far from Samaria.

9.50.1.en: Be concerned with positive action and gentleness in dealing with others, even if they wrong you, finding excuses for them.

9.51.0.en: Many were influenced by Christ's teachings, and one of them said to Him that he wanted to follow Him, that is, to become one of His disciples, but God, who knows what is in hearts, answered him, revealing what was in his heart, since he regarded Christ, like the rest of the Jews, as an earthly king, and wanted to follow Him to obtain glory and wealth.

9.51.1.en: Christ said to him that the foxes and the birds have places to which they resort, but He has no particular house in which to lodge, that is, He does not even own a place like the animals and the birds, and consequently whoever follows Him must strip himself of the love of money and earthly glory.

9.51.2.en: The foxes point to craftiness and the birds to pride, because they soar on high, so the spiritual person must be freed from craftiness and pride, so that Christ may find a place within him in which to rest.

9.52.0.en: Christ found a person who had a spiritual readiness for spiritual discipleship and service, so He said to him, Follow me, to reveal one of the hindrances of his following, since he answered Christ in the affirmative, that is, agreeing to follow Him, but first asked permission to bury his father and put off following Jesus.

9.52.1.en: What is meant here by burying is caring for his aged father until he dies and burying him, or what is meant is the rites of mourning for the dead, which may extend for months, and not merely the act of burial; for God commanded honoring parents and consequently attention to their burial.

9.52.2.en: Christ answered by rejecting this postponement, and made clear that caring for people more than God is a failure to appreciate His love, so God ought to be obeyed more than people, and the one who does not understand and appreciate the importance of salvation and service is dead spiritually; therefore He said, Let the dead (spiritually) bury their dead (physically), that is, those absorbed in material things are occupied with the rites of mourning or emotional relationships, but you ought to care for the salvation of your soul before everything, which is achieved through your service to God and preaching His Kingdom.

9.53.0.en: The third case is a person who wanted to follow Christ but was hesitating between following Him and his attachment to his family. The young man does not mean by farewell that he would greet them, for that does not take a long time, but means that he would spend many days with them, and he might not be able to leave them because of emotional attachment, and consequently would not follow Christ.

9.53.1.en: Christ's answer to him was the parable of the plowman, who cannot complete his work unless he concentrates on looking ahead to the end of the field that he will reach with the plow, pressing on it with his foot to do his work successfully; but if he looks behind him, the plow goes in crooked directions, and will not break the ground to the depth required.

9.53.2.en: What is meant here is that whoever is occupied with the world, material things and emotional relationships more than with God, they will make him hesitant and even hinder him from following Christ.

9.53.3.en: Christ rejoices in your following Him, if you seek no aim but Him and are not occupied with material things or human relationships more than with Him; then you are able to love God and love all people.

9.53.4.en: The mission of the Apostles and the good Samaritan
